summary.one_liner: Snip is a visual review tool for Claude Code and other AI coding agents: agents render diagrams or UI previews, you annotate them on screen, and the agent gets structured feedback, and it also works as a local screenshot and annotation app.
summary.what_it_does: Snip runs as a menu bar or system tray app with a CLI that AI coding agents can call. The agent can render a Mermaid diagram, HTML, or UI component to an image with `snip render`, and the user approves it or annotates it with circles, arrows, and notes. Review commands (`render`, `open`) block until the user finishes and return structured JSON the agent can act on. An MCP server exposes the same capabilities for agents without shell access. Snip is also a standalone screenshot tool with region and window capture, a clipboard quick-capture, and annotation tools (rectangle, arrow, text, tag, blur, AI segment). Saved screenshots can be organized by a local vision LLM via Ollama and searched semantically by description. The README says core AI features run locally without cloud APIs.
use_cases: review AI-generated diagrams before code is written
annotate screenshots and send feedback to a coding agent
render Mermaid architecture or ER diagrams from Claude Code
preview UI components rendered by an agent
capture and annotate screenshots on macOS or Linux
search a local screenshot library by description
how_to_run: npm run rebuild # compile native modules (macOS)
notable: Visual feedback loop: the agent renders output, the user annotates it on screen, and the agent receives structured feedback to iterate
Works via CLI commands or an MCP server
Doubles as a standalone screenshot and annotation app with quick-to-clipboard capture
Local AI organization and semantic search of screenshots using Ollama and a vision model
Documentation covers product, design, architecture, devops, and user flows
caveats: Requires macOS 14+ or Linux (Wayland); Windows is not mentioned
Needs Node.js 18+ and native module compilation for development
AI organization depends on a local Ollama install
The README includes a sponsorship appeal for Apple Developer and CI costs, which suggests ongoing funding needs
